title: Attention bias towards pictures of self-perceived migraine triggers in patients with migraine compared to neutral pictures and healthy control participants – a cross-sectional international online study
summary:
Background:
Many people with migraine report that certain things, such as foods, drinks, changes in weather, or stress, trigger their headaches. However, it is not yet clear whether these things actually cause headaches. It is also possible that some of these experiences are already part of the early signs of an upcoming migraine attack. As a result, people with migraine may pay more attention to certain things.

Research question:
This study aims to investigate whether people with migraine pay more attention to pictures of things that they themselves perceive as triggers for their headaches compared with neutral pictures. It will also examine whether people with migraine differ from people without headaches in how they respond to these pictures and whether the results differ between different regions of the world.

Methods:
The study will be conducted entirely online and will take approximately 30 to 45 minutes. About 138 people will take part, with approximately half having migraine and the other half having no headaches. First, participants will answer questions about themselves and their headaches. The participants will then complete a task a computer task in which they will see different pictures while trying to identify a specific letter as quickly as possible. The pictures will either show neutral content or things that may trigger headaches. The study will measure how quickly and how accurately participants respond. At the end, participants will indicate which of the things shown they personally perceive as triggers for their headaches. Participation takes place only once. No medication will be administered, and no headaches or migraine attacks will be deliberately induced.

interventions.name:
Migraine group:
- required to complete the Headache Screening Questionnaire and HIT-6 once
- need to provide information on their self-perceived migraine triggers once 
- need to complete a Perceptual Load Task once

Control group:
- need to confirm that they do not meet the ICDH migraine criteria 
- need to complete a Perceptual Load Task once

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
≥18 years; informed consent; migraine diagnosis with or without aura for the migraine group; no more than two headache days per month and no migraine criteria for controls; sufficient understanding of German, English, Spanish or Portuguese; and ability to complete the computer-based task using a physical keyboard.
Exclusion criteria:
age <18 years; absence of informed consent; failure to meet group-specific eligibility criteria; inability to complete the computer task; incomplete or insufficient task data; or clearly duplicated/invalid datasets identified during quality control.
